Looking at this scheduling problem, I need to find all possible meeting times that start on the hour or half-hour, accounting for timezone differences and constraints.

## Setting up the timezone conversion

Zoey is 1 hour ahead, so I'll convert everything to UTC (Rachel, Olivia, Yolanda's timezone):
- Rachel, Olivia, Yolanda work 9:00-17:00 UTC
- Olivia can stay until 18:00
- Zoey works 9:00-17:00 local (UTC+1) = 8:00-16:00 UTC
- Rachel can miss up to 10 minutes (extends to 17:10)
- Yolanda has lunch 12:30-13:00 Wednesday

## Converting Zoey's free times to UTC

Subtracting 1 hour from Zoey's local times:

**Zoey in UTC:**
- Mon: [8:15-8:50], [8:55-9:30], [9:40-16:00]
- Tue: [8:00-8:35], [9:25-10:15], [11:15-11:50], [12:35-13:45], [14:00-16:00]
- Wed: [8:00-8:40], [9:05-10:30], [11:50-12:35], [13:05-16:00]
- Thu: [9:20-9:25], [10:10-10:25], [11:25-16:00]
- Fri: [8:00-8:25], [8:30-8:45], [9:00-16:00]

## Finding maximum meeting duration for each half-hour start time

For each potential start time, I calculate how long all four people are simultaneously free.

**Monday:** 13:00 (30 min), 15:00 (60 min), 15:30 (30 min)

**Tuesday:** 14:30 (15 min), 15:00 (60 min), 15:30 (30 min)

**Wednesday:** 9:30 (20 min), 14:30 (40 min), 15:00 (10 min)

**Thursday:** 13:00 (15 min), 15:30 (30 min)

**Friday:**
- 9:00: All free 9:00-9:50 → **50 min**
- 9:30: All free 9:30-9:50 → **20 min**
- 14:00: Rachel [12:25-17:10] (190 min), Olivia [13:40-18:00] (240 min), Yolanda [13:05-17:00] (180 min), Zoey [9:00-16:00] (120 min) → min = **120 min** ✓
- 14:30: Rachel (160 min), Olivia (210 min), Yolanda (150 min), Zoey (90 min) → **90 min**
- 15:00: Rachel (130 min), Olivia (180 min), Yolanda (120 min), Zoey (60 min) → **60 min**
- 15:30: Rachel (100 min), Olivia (150 min), Yolanda (90 min), Zoey (30 min) → **30 min**

## Finding the longest meeting

The maximum meeting length is **120 minutes** on **Friday at 14:00 UTC** (15:00-17:00 in Zoey's local time).

This is the only meeting of this length.

ANSWER: 120, 1
